To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
PEM surface functionalization of PDMS microfluidic devices is suitable for the prevention of nonspecific cell attachment and that PEG-based terminal layers further reduce the cell adhesion strength.
the PEM surface modifications significantly reduced yeast cell adhesion strength in PDMS microfluidic devices.
a facile layer by layer surface functionalization from water-based solutions can be successfully used to decrease cell adhesion strength by at least 2 orders of magnitude compared with bare PDMS.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a simple and versatile method for the surface functionalization of microfluidic devices with the aim to reduce nonspecific cell adhesion.
the design of a novel, easy to handle surface functionalization strategy for PDMS-based microdevices that can be applied for a broad spectrum of microorganism types.
the development of a new approach to functionalize the inner surface of microfluidic channels with a view to reduce the nonspecific attachment of cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the PEM surface functionalization of PDMS microfluidic devices can be successfully used to decrease the adhesion of hydrophobic S. cerevisae cells by at least two magnitudes compared to bare PDMDMS surfaces.
the PAA-g-PEC layer is more effective to reduce the yeast attachment strength than the PAH/PAA and PDADMAC/PAA multilayers, respectively.
the PEMs are able to decrease cell adhesion strength by a factor of 10, whereas the additional PAA-g-peg layer is able to further reduce the adhesion strength by another factor of 10.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of PEMs with the PAA-g- PEG copolymer is a promising approach for reducing nonspecific cell adhesion to the surface of PDMS-based microdevices.
the combination of PEMs and PAA-g-PEGSurface functionalization of PDMS can be used for the development of a new generation of PDMS-based microsystems for cell cultivation and analysis.
the PEM modification of PDMS is a suitable method to reduce nonspecific cell adhesion in PDMS-based devices.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PEMs can be applied as a universal surface modification method for microfluidic devices, which are intended for the growth of hydrophobic cells.

the surface functionalization by layer-by-layer assembly of polyelectrolytes and subsequent adsorption of copolymers containing PEG side chains can be applied to reduce cell attachment in microfluidic systems.
the PEMs can be used to modify the surface of PDMS-based microdevices to promote cell growth and to reduce nonspecific cell adhesion.
